body:
Resolve: https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/40460

Problem:
There is no shared utility for turning an filesystem-unsafe string into a safe filename, so each subsystem makes its own encoding and plugins reinvent the same wheel.

Solution:
add `vim.fs.slug()`, which generates a bounded, one-way filename from an arbitrary string. The result depends on whether it fits `opts.maxlen`: name that fits is only sanitized; a longer name becomes "{head}-~~~-{tail}-{hash8}".

comment_data.body: Is it safe to use a Unicode char here? Maybe a simple `---` would be more robust.
comment_data.diff_hunk:
@@ -147,6 +147,144 @@ function M.joinpath(...)
   return (path:gsub(iswin and '[/\\][/\\]*' or '//+', '/'))
 end
 
+--- Built-in prefix map for `opts.map`
+---@type table<string, string>?
+local prefix_map
+
+--- @return table<string, string>
+local function get_prefix_map()
+  if not prefix_map then
+    prefix_map = {
+      [vim.fn.stdpath('data')] = '=data',
+      [vim.fn.stdpath('state')] = '=state',
+      [vim.fn.stdpath('cache')] = '=cache',
+      [vim.fn.stdpath('config')] = '=config',
+      [uv.os_homedir() or '~'] = '~',
+    }
+  end
+  return prefix_map
+end
+
+--- Windows reserved basenames (case-insensitive).
+--- Ref: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/fileio/naming-a-file
+local win_reserved_names = {
+  con = true,
+  prn = true,
+  aux = true,
+  nul = true,
+  com1 = true,
+  com2 = true,
+  com3 = true,
+  com4 = true,
+  com5 = true,
+  com6 = true,
+  com7 = true,
+  com8 = true,
+  com9 = true,
+  ['com¹'] = true,
+  ['com²'] = true,
+  ['com³'] = true,
+  lpt1 = true,
+  lpt2 = true,
+  lpt3 = true,
+  lpt4 = true,
+  lpt5 = true,
+  lpt6 = true,
+  lpt7 = true,
+  lpt8 = true,
+  lpt9 = true,
+  ['lpt¹'] = true,
+  ['lpt²'] = true,
+  ['lpt³'] = true,
+}
+
+--- Generates a bounded, filesystem-safe filename from an arbitrary identity string.
+---
+--- - Each unsafe character (`/ \ : * ? " < > |`, whitespace, control characters) is replaced with
+---   "-" and trailing "-" and "." are stripped.
+--- - Windows reserved basenames get a "-" appended at the stem ("con.txt" => "con-.txt").
+--- - If the result exceeds `opts.maxlen` bytes it becomes "{head}-…-{tail}-{hash8}": middle

+--- Generates a bounded, filesystem-safe filename from an arbitrary identity string.
+---
+--- - Each unsafe character (`/ \ : * ? " < > |`, whitespace, control characters) is replaced with
+---   "-" and trailing "-" and "." are stripped.
+--- - Windows reserved basenames get a "-" appended at the stem ("con.txt" => "con-.txt").
+--- - If the result exceeds `opts.maxlen` bytes it becomes "{head}-…-{tail}-{hash8}": middle
+---   segments are elided at "-" boundaries and 8 hex chars of the |sha256()| of the full `path`
+---   keep it unique. The hash appears only when truncated.
+---
+--- Examples:
+---
+--- ```lua
+--- vim.fs.slug('/home/foo/.config/nvim/init.lua')
+--- -- => "-home-foo-.config-nvim-init.lua"
+---
+--- vim.fs.slug('C:/Users/me/foo/file.txt')
+--- -- => "C--Users-me-foo-file.txt"
+---
+--- vim.fs.slug(('/a/very/long/path'):rep(10) .. '/file.txt', { maxlen = 60 })
+--- -- => "-a-very-long-…-path-a-very-long-path-file.txt-405cfe4a"
+---
+--- vim.fs.slug(vim.fn.stdpath('state') .. '/term', { map = true })
+--- -- => "=state-term"
+--- ```
+---
+---@since 13

comment_data.body:
🤔Interesting point. Could you explain more about why it's unsafe?

Although @justinmk proposed `…` back in the issue, I indeed thought about using `---`. But I still chose `…` in the end because we've used `-` to replace unsafe chars, thus using `---` here would cause ambiguity. `---` can be easily constructed, for example, `vim.fs.slug('foo - bar')` => `foo---bar`. And any other ASCII char is either unsafe or likely to be used in a file / path name.

comment_data.body: It's just an unnecessary possible point of failure with different filesystem encodings. As the point of this function is to replace possibly unsafe chars with known safe chars, this strikes me as a step in the opposite direction.
